📦 Measuring Warehouse Utilization

Capstone project for the Robotics Systems Engineering programme at SIT. The system uses overhead cameras and computer vision to provide continuous, automated monitoring of warehouse staging zone floor space — replacing manual audits with real-time data.

The Problem

Warehouse staging areas lack automated visibility into floor space utilization. Manual audits are infrequent, labour-intensive, and produce stale data — preventing managers from optimizing pallet placement or identifying congestion before it happens.

The Solution

A stationary overhead camera system using YOLOv8 object detection and ArUco marker-based zone calibration. The team pivoted from the original AMR-based brief to a fixed camera approach — delivering continuous monitoring at a fraction of the cost, with no navigation complexity and no safety risk to floor workers.

1:16 Scale Prototype

The physical prototype uses aluminum framing, a plywood base spray-painted grey to simulate a factory floor, and an acrylic ceiling panel with a string-hoist system for adjustable camera height. The camera sits at 57 cm — equivalent to a real-world ceiling height of 9.12 m at 1:16 scale.

Flask Dashboard

The web-based dashboard at localhost:5000 displays combined and per-zone utilization gauges, an occupancy grid with bird's-eye view, pallet breakdowns by type (EU/US, empty/loaded), a utilization trend chart, and CSV export — all updating on 30-second snapshot cycles.

YOLOv8 Object Detection

The custom YOLOv8 model detects and classifies pallets (EU/US, empty/loaded), humans, and forklifts in real time. Bounding boxes show class labels, confidence scores, and in-zone/outside status. A three-stage inclusion check (centroid, base midpoint, 30% overlap) determines whether partially overlapping pallets count toward zone utilization.

YOLOv8 Training Results

The model was trained on 1,121+ manually annotated images across 9 classes and validated on a 217-image test set. It achieved an overall mAP50 of 0.987 and mAP50-95 of 0.962, with per-class precision consistently above 0.80 and inference speed of approximately 4.7 ms per image on an RTX 5070 Laptop GPU.

ArUco Zone Detection & Calibration

Four ArUco markers (DICT_4X4_50) placed at zone corners define the staging boundary. A camera calibration step using a 5×5 ArUco board corrects lens distortion, and a homography transformation warps the angled camera view into a bird's-eye perspective — enabling accurate real-world area measurement in square metres despite the 20° camera tilt.

Technologies Used

YOLOv8 ROS2 Python OpenCV Flask ArUco Markers Homography Orbbec Dabai

Outcome

Delivered a fully functional prototype at SGD $158 — approximately 87% below the initial estimate. The system achieved detection accuracy of mAP50 = 0.987 and met all project objectives for accuracy, update frequency, and deployability.
